why:
phase-482 W4 (2026-10-07): on `rclcpp_lifecycle::LifecycleNode` too, forwarding to the engine; `register_on_*` takes `CallbackReturn (*)(const State&, void*)` plus a context, not a `std::function`.

Before phase-482 W4: RE-VERDICTED phase-417 W4.f. was `gap`, and the row's own reading was right: the table was already `const` in `nros-node/src/lifecycle_services.rs` and served over `~/get_transition_graph`, and no language could read it in process. It MOVED rather than being copied -- `nros_core::lifecycle::LifecycleTransition::{ALL,label_cstr,source_state,goal_state}` is the one table now, `lifecycle_services` aliases it, C reaches it through `rclc_lifecycle_transition_graph` and friends, and `nros::Transition` stores an id and asks. So a node and a remote `ros2 lifecycle list` cannot disagree about the graph. THE DIVERGENCE: upstream returns `std::vector<Transition>`; ours VISITS (`get_transition_graph(visit, ctx)`), because there is no allocator to hand a container back from and the visitor is the vocabulary every other query on this class already uses. Deliberately NOT an `nros::Span` over the static table, which fits better and would newly expose `Span` / `StringView` / `LeSpan` on the public C++ surface as a side effect -- `graph.hpp` and `options.hpp` each declined that for the same reason (16 unledgered items, measured), and it stays a decision for whoever classifies those types.
